newsitem.title: USA: Lee Enterprises sells unit for $55 million.
newsitem.headline: Lee Enterprises sells unit for $55 million.

text.p: Lee Enterprises Inc. said Friday it sold NAPP Systems Inc., its graphic arts products subsidiary, to Polyfibron Technologies Inc. for $55 million.
NAPP, based in San Marcos, Calif., provides photopolymer printing plates and processing systems to the newspaper industry worldwide.
Lee, based in Davenport, Iowa, said the sale permits it to concentrate on its core media business. It said NAPP remains an important supplier for some of its newspapers.
Lee owns publishes 19 daily newspapers and 40 weekly and speciality publications and operates nine affiliated television stations and seven satellite television stations.

Polyfibron is a closely held company based in Billerica, Mass., that was founded in 1994 to acquire the printing products business of W.R. Grace & Co. With the acquisition of NAPP, Polyfibron will have annual revenues of more than $200 million.
Lee's stock was unchanged at $23.125 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.
